content:
iCloud+ includes much more than just extra storage space, and one of the perks exclusive to subscribers — custom email domains — has recently become even more useful.

iCloud+ subscribers can now create up to 10 personalised email addresses using a custom domain

When creating a new email account, you can always choose the standard @gmail.com or @icloud.com domain. But there are actually even more personalised options available.

Third-party services offer custom email addresses, but they require a monthly fee. However, many people may not realise that as long as you own your own domain, iCloud+ can help you set up a custom email address for free.

Through iCloud+, you can set up email addresses that end with personalised wording or terms related to your business. This is one of iCloud+'s most underappreciated perks, and it has now become even more useful.

As pdfu pointed out on X, Apple has now increased the number of email addresses that can be created per custom domain.

iCloud+ now allows up to 10 personalised email addresses to be set up per custom domain.

Previously, you could only set up 3 personalised addresses per domain. Increasing it to 10 is a big leap, especially for those who run their own businesses, who should find it very useful. I've also noticed that quite a few families set up custom domains for their household members, and this new higher limit is also very helpful for such uses.

iCloud+'s custom email domain feature is available to all subscribers — you can learn how to set it up here.

Are you using custom email addresses with your iCloud+ subscription? Feel free to let us know in the comments.
